symptoms: Small brown spots with a yellow ring appear on the leaves.
Older leaves may drop off the plant.
Small water-soaked spots appear on green fruit.
These spots grow into raised, rough, and scabby sores.
The centers of the sores turn light brown and sink in.
favourable_conditions: Moist weather, heavy rainstorms, high humidity, or persistent dew help the disease spread.
prevention: Always use seeds and seedlings that are free of disease.
Rotate your tomato crop with plants that do not catch this disease.
Avoid planting in areas where you grew tomatoes last year to keep away from old plant trash.
practices: Remove and destroy any plant parts that show signs of the disease.
Clear away old plant debris from the field to stop the spread.
Monitor your plants closely for new spots.
